source_text:
Contra Severum Antiochenum (fragmentum ap. Pseudo-Anastasium
Sinaitam, Contra monophysitas)
89.1189 Ὀλυμπιοδώρου τοῦ μεγάλου φιλοσόφου διακόνου Ἀλεξανδρείας, ἐκ τοῦ
δευτέρου λόγου τοῦ κατὰ Σεβήρου, ἐν ᾧ παραγαγὼν τὴν χρῆσιν τοῦ ἁγίου
Ἀθανασίου τὴν λέγουσαν τὰ δύο θελήματα ἐπὶ Χριστοῦ, οὕτω πως διεξέρχεται
λέγων·
orientation: This is the introductory lemma identifying the author, work, and the Athanasius quotation about two wills in Christ that Olympiodorus is about to expound.
pass_a_gloss: Of Olympiodorus the great philosopher, deacon of Alexandria, from the second book of the work against Severus, in which, having brought forward the quotation of Saint Athanasius that says the two wills in the case of Christ, Olympiodorus expounds it in some such way, saying:

choices.why: The glossary requires 'book' for λόγος in the sense of a division of a multi-part work.
The glossary requires 'quotation' for χρῆσις as a quoted passage from an authority.
The glossary requires 'wills' for θελήματα, specifically the two wills in Christ.
ἐπί with genitive here means 'in the case of' or 'with reference to,' preserving the locative force without over-interpreting.

pass_b_english: From the second book of Olympiodorus, the great philosopher and deacon of Alexandria, against Severus. In it, after bringing forward the quotation from Saint Athanasius that speaks of two wills in the case of Christ, he goes through it in this way, saying:

problems.quote: he expounds it in this way, saying
problems.why: Same Greek verb rendered differently; reader may think actions differ
